blocks.orig: Asanja Moru is a bush camp set among rocky islands known as Moru Kopjes in the eastern part of Serengeti National Park. The camp boasts 8 ensuite tents (among which one spacious family tent) all slightly differently decorated in a combination of whitewashed and dark woods and natural fabrics, with comfy furniture and an outside terrace with a (of course!) a view. The Moru Kopjes area is well-known as the place where the migrating herds pass by on their way down south, with Gong Rock (a slab of rock with a metallic sound that you can hit like a drum) nearby and the salty Lake Magadi with its flamingos to the east. A lovely place to rest your head for the night!
blocks.html: Asanja Moru is a bush camp among the rocky outcrops called Moru Kopjes, in the east of Serengeti National Park. The camp has 8 ensuite tents (one of them a roomy family tent), each decorated a little differently using a mix of whitewashed and dark woods and natural fabrics, with comfortable furniture and an outdoor terrace with (naturally!) a view. The Moru Kopjes area is known as the spot where the migrating herds pass through on their journey south, with Gong Rock nearby (a rock slab that makes a metallic sound you can strike like a drum) and the salty Lake Magadi with its flamingos to the east. A lovely spot to spend the night!
